rationale: diagnose_load_runtime reads diagnose_route's forwarded requests and upstream drop counts under the 'route.' namespace by string; diagnose_route writes them under ITS output_field. Nothing tied the two ends together, so a per-workflow override of the route step's output_field (or of the reader's *_field config) makes every route.* read resolve to nothing — a forwarded request or an upstream drop is then silently counted as ZERO, re-opening exactly the silence the drop reporting exists to close (council trail eba040a9 round 5 left this open as a design decision; the spin guard credits a code/data request as progress on the promise its answer arrives next gather, and a silent drop breaks that promise with nothing in the trail). The originally proposed fix — 'check the field exists in collected_data before trusting its absence' — was investigated and DOES NOT WORK: (1) the writer only writes route.code_requests_dropped when dropped>0, so absence is the NORMAL zero-drops case; (2) an output_field override moves route.diagnose_state and route.iteration too, erasing the only signals that would distinguish 'route ran elsewhere' from 'iteration 1, route has not run yet'; (3) the reader cannot see a sibling step's config — ActionParams carried only its own StepConfig. The honest fix is to let the reader see the writer's actual configured output_field and compare directly, once, at the first gather — fail loudly on divergence instead of running the whole loop blind. NOTE: this change is committed (6f7e69d22) and live in v1.0.1151; this is the review the owner asked for on it — objections will be applied forward as follow-up commits.

plan.summary: Thread the workflow plan's step map into ActionParams (read-only, additive) so an action can validate a name-based coupling to a sibling step the compiler cannot see; have diagnose_load_runtime assert on each gather that its four route-coupled *_field config values name a namespace some diagnose_route step actually writes under. A consistent override (both ends moved together) passes; only a divergence fails, loudly, before the loop runs blind. Fails open on a nil step map or a workflow with no route step. Falsification-tested: divergent, partial and empty-output_field wirings all fail; default and consistent-override pass.

edits.rationale: The reader cannot validate a coupling to a sibling step it cannot see. Additive field; nil-safe; no other action uses it.
Populate the new field from state the coordinator already holds. One line; no behaviour change for actions that ignore it.

edits.rationale: The check itself. Collects every output_field any diagnose_route step writes under; asserts each of the reader's four route-coupled *_field values (data_requests_field, code_requests_field, and the two *_dropped_field) names one of those namespaces. Kept in the READER (it validates its own contract) rather than teaching the generic coordinator a diagnose-specific invariant.

Call the guard BEFORE any route.* read, so a mismatch fails the FIRST gather rather than running the whole loop blind (the loop's gather_step re-enters here each iteration, so the check also covers mid-run plan mutation).

Falsification tests, not happy-path: the guard's job is to catch a fault, so the tests INDUCE the fault and confirm the catch. Seven cases: default passes; consistent override passes; divergent override FAILS naming the present namespace; partial single-field override FAILS; empty route output_field FAILS (route stores nothing); no route step skips; nil steps fail open.

grounded_in: diagnose_route_action.go:301-302 — the writer only writes the drop key on drops: `if droppedCR > 0 { result[codeRequestsDroppedKey] = droppedCR`  — so field-absence is the NORMAL zero case and cannot signal broken wiring

diagnose_route_action.go:206-207 — an output_field override moves the disambiguators too: `"diagnose_state": diagnose.EncodeLoopState(&st), "iteration": st.Iteration` are written into the same result map, so the reader has no override-independent signal

diagnose_route_action.go:317-323 (comment) — 'these are a name-based coupling ACROSS action boundaries with no schema or compile-time tie, so a rename at one end would silently re-open exactly the silence this reporting exists to close (council-gate eba040a9, bug_historian)'

diagnose_load_runtime_action.go:352-353 — the vulnerable read: `codeDropField := datahelpers.GetStringField(config, "code_requests_dropped_field", routeOutputPrefix+codeRequestsDroppedKey)` then `GetIntField(params.CollectedData, codeDropField, 0)` — absence and zero are indistinguishable

plan.risks: 1) A LEGITIMATE exotic wiring could be blocked: a workflow that deliberately points a *_field at a non-route namespace (e.g. a static test fixture injected via input_data) would now fail at gather — mitigations: the check only fires when a diagnose_route step EXISTS in the plan, and a consistent rename passes; no live workflow does this today (the only diagnose workflow uses the defaults). 2) The check runs every gather iteration, not once — cost is a map scan over ~20 steps, negligible. 3) ActionParams gains a field other actions can now read: widens the action-side surface to the whole plan (read-only); a future action could grow an unwanted dependency on sibling steps — the field's comment constrains intent but nothing enforces it. 4) Tests construct models.Step directly; if Step gains required invariants the fixtures could drift from real plans. Reviewers should check: is fail-open on nil WorkflowSteps right (a caller that forgets to populate it silently loses the guard), and should the guard also cover the route step's own state_field read-back (route.diagnose_state), which has the same coupling shape but is read by the route step itself rather than the reader.
